Package hadur2.core.knn

Class KnnView<T>

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.knn.KnnView<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the value logged with each point: a firing angle for the gun, a guess factor for the surf
public class KnnView<T> extends Object
One KNN "view" of an opponent: a feature space (its DistanceFormula), a bounded KdTree of past wave outcomes in that space, and the settings that say which waves it learns from and how many neighbours it returns.

The gun keeps a main view and four anti-surfer views per opponent (hadur2.core.gun.GunController); the surf keeps its danger and flattener views (hadur2.core.move.MoveController). When a wave breaks, the owner calls logWave(Wave, Object) with where the target went; when it aims or surfs, it calls nearestNeighbors(Wave, boolean) and combines the neighbours' values into a density. Views are built with the fluent setters, which return the view.

Invariants: the tree's dimension is formula.weights.length, and the tree never holds more than maxDataPoints points, or DEFAULT_MAX_DATA_POINTS when that is 0 (RES-2). Samples replayed from an opponent profile go in through logSeed(double[], Object, SeedWeight) and carry a shared SeedWeight (ADAPT-3); effectiveSize() stops counting them once that weight reaches 0 (RES-4).

    • cachedNeighbors

      public Map<Integer,List<KdTree.Entry<T>>> cachedNeighbors
      The surf's neighbour lists by surf wave index (0 for the first wave it surfs), so a wave's neighbours are searched once while the surf scores many candidate positions against it. The surf clears it through clearCache() whenever the wave it surfs changes, and both owners clear it at each round's start, which bounds it (RES-2).

    • NO_DECAY

      public static final double NO_DECAY
      A decayRate that gives every neighbour weight 1.

    • DEFAULT_MAX_DATA_POINTS

      public static final int DEFAULT_MAX_DATA_POINTS
      Cap for views that set no limit of their own (RES-2). It sits above what a 35-round battle collects, so normal battles behave exactly as if unbounded.

    • logSeed

      public void logSeed(double[] dataPoint, T value, SeedWeight weight)
      Adds a sample replayed from an opponent profile (ADAPT-3). The point must already be in this view's formula space; the value carries the seed's weight.

      All seeds in one view are expected to share one weight; the last one given is the one effectiveSize() reads. The point is copied, so the caller may reuse its array and the tree's eviction (by array identity) still finds each point.

      Parameters:
      dataPoint - the sample's features, formula.weights.length values
      value - the outcome, carrying the same weight
      weight - the weight the seeds share
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the point has the wrong number of dimensions

    • logDataPoint

    • thresholdsMet

      public boolean thresholdsMet(double hitPercentage, double marginOfError)
      Whether an enemy hit percentage and its margin clear this view's thresholds.

      The rate itself must reach hitThreshold, and the rate less its margin (floored at 0) must reach paddedHitThreshold: a view gated on the padded threshold waits until the rate is certainly high enough (DIAL-1).

      Parameters:
      hitPercentage - the enemy's hit percentage, 0 to 100
      marginOfError - its margin of error, in percentage points
      Returns:
      true when both thresholds are met

    • size

      public int size()
      The points held, seeds included, after eviction; at most the cap (RES-2).

    • effectiveSize

      public int effectiveSize()
      Samples that still carry weight: size() less the seeds once their weight has fallen to zero (RES-4). The tree evicts oldest first and seeds go in first, so evicted points are counted against the seeds.

      The gun reads this for its warm-up thresholds, so a faded seed leaves the gun as cold as it would be without one.

      Returns:
      the number of points that still count, never negative

    • setWeights

      public void setWeights(double[] weights)
      Replaces the per-axis weights in the formula and the tree. A formula shared by several views (the anti-surfer gun's) gets the new array for all of them, while only this view's tree does.
      Parameters:
      weights - one weight per dimension

    • getDecayWeights

      public Map<Timestamped,Double> getDecayWeights(List<? extends KdTree.Entry<? extends Timestamped>> entries)
      Time-decay weights for a neighbour list: the newest entry weighs 1 and each older one decayRate times less than the next newer; with NO_DECAY every entry weighs 1. Entries are ordered by round, then tick, so seeds (filed under Timestamped.SEED_ROUND) count as the oldest.
      Parameters:
      entries - the neighbours, as a search returned them
      Returns:
      each entry's value mapped to its weight, keyed by identity
